reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) does not directly support the key premises. E2 discusses hot cracking in a different alloy (CoCrFeNiCu) without preheating, and E3 describes an alternative binder-based AM method, not LPBF preheating. The premises about preheating's effects on thermal gradients, segregation, and stress relaxation in AlCrFeNiSi are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Preheating substrate to ~600 °C reduces thermal gradients in LPBF
Reduced thermal gradients lower cooling rates and thermal stresses
Lower cooling rates minimize elemental partitioning and segregation
Reduced thermal stresses prevent hot cracking and allow stress relaxation
These effects collectively improve mechanical integrity (strength and ductility)
